$comment: Root Deno 2.x workspace. Members are added here as each package is scaffolded. Path aliases per documentation/architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md §2. Do NOT list a member directory that does not yet exist — Deno errors on missing members.

tasks.$comment:dev: Two dev modes, one flag. `dev` pins USE_MOCKS=false so the name is a guarantee rather than a hope — it serves whatever each *_BACKEND_LIVE gate in .env allows, which is the database. `dev:mock` pins it true, which overrides every gate at once and serves fixtures. The prefix wins over .env because apps/web/main.ts calls dotenv load({export:true}), and that never overwrites a variable the process already has (verified, not assumed). Deno task shell supports POSIX env prefixes on Windows too, so this needs no cross-env dependency.
tasks.$comment:build: One pass builds everything. The workspace members (packages/types, packages/ui, packages/backend) have NO separate compile step — they are consumed as TypeScript source through the import map, so Vite type-strips and bundles them alongside the app. `vite build` drives both Fresh environments: the client environment emits the island bundles into _fresh/client, the ssr environment emits the route chunks + _fresh/server.js. There is nothing to build before it and nothing to build after it.
tasks.$comment:serve: Runs an EXISTING production build. `_fresh/server.js` is written by @fresh/plugin-vite and default-exports { fetch }, which is exactly the shape `deno serve` expects. `--unstable-kv` is not required — FxService feature-detects `Deno.openKv` and falls back to a per-isolate memory cache — but without it the 15-minute FX rate cache is lost on every isolate.
tasks.$comment:start: Build, then start the production SSR server. This is the single self-contained entry point: `deno task start`.
tasks.start: deno task build && deno task serve
tasks.$comment:check: Entry points, not `deno check .`: the latter walks build output and any stray git worktree under .claude/, which is not this repo's code. The routes globs are NOT redundant with `apps/web/main.ts`: routes are discovered from the filesystem at runtime and are in NO module's import graph, so before they were listed here `deno task check` type-checked not one of the ~200 route files — a whole class of error (a route calling a fat-service method that does not exist, a handler returning the wrong shape) passed the merge gate silently. Verified by measurement: with the graph-only form, `deno check apps/web/main.ts` exits 0 while `deno check apps/web/routes/api/projects/setup.ts` reports the missing method. `**` is expanded by the task shell, on Windows too.
tasks.$comment:test: The merge gate. `--allow-env` is needed because the backend env reader is pulled in transitively by anything touching a service; `--allow-read` for module loading.
tasks.test: deno task check && deno task lint && deno task test:unit
tasks.$comment:fmt: Deliberately NOT part of `test`, for two reasons that are facts about this repo rather than preferences. (1) `core.autocrlf=true` means a Windows checkout has CRLF in the working tree while `deno fmt` wants LF, so `--check` reports every file as unformatted there no matter what anyone commits. (2) ~280 files predate the formatter, and reformatting them wholesale would bury real diffs. Format the files you touch (`deno fmt <paths>`) rather than the tree.
